chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Razi, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Abu Ayoob, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever makes his tongue truthful, his deeds become pure; and whoever has good intention, God will increase his sustenance; and whoever treats his family kindly, God will extend his life.
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that lead to increased sustenance and extended life according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a causal link between internal sincerity and external divine favor, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (purity of intention) as the foundation of righteous action. It highlights the holistic nature of Islamic ethics, where truthfulness purifies the self, good intention invites material provision (*rizq*), and familial piety (*birr*) serves as a means for longevity.
